cues.text: June 1812. Napoleon crosses the River Niemen, into Russia.
By one famous count, he has 422,000 men.
The Russians fall back, and burn what they leave behind.
Napoleon follows them east. Vitebsk. Smolensk. Borodino.
Heat, sickness, desertion and battle cost him men at every step.
In September he reaches Moscow, with about 100,000 left.
The city burns. The Tsar refuses to talk peace.
In October, the army turns back. Then winter comes.
Snow, hunger and Cossacks, all the way to the river.
About 10,000 make it back across the Niemen.
